title: Settings
subtitle: Connections, paths, models, limits and access

status.title: Status
status.summary: Summary as the agent sees it

doctor.title: Doctor
doctor.description: Checks connections, paths, hard links, permissions, space and indexers.
doctor.askFixPrompt_one: Doctor found {{count}} problem: {{list}}. Please help me fix it.
doctor.askFixPrompt_other: Doctor found {{count}} problems: {{list}}. Please help me fix them.

paths.title: Paths
paths.description: Where media lives, as Reelix sees it. Downloads and library must be on the same file system for hard links.

downloader.title: Downloader
downloader.description: The torrent client Reelix uses. Only you choose it; when it is off or broken, downloads stop with a clear message and Reelix never switches to another by itself. Its own address and password are on its plugin page.
downloader.activeHelp: Every downloader plugin that is switched on and set up is listed.
downloader.notRunning: The downloader "{{id}}" is not running: switch its plugin on and set it up under Plugins, or choose another.
downloader.pathMapHelp: How the downloader names the same folders: {{example}}

mediaServer.title: Media server
mediaServer.description: The media server Reelix tells about filed and removed files, and whose watch history shapes suggestions. Only you choose it; it is optional. Its own address and key are on its plugin page.
mediaServer.activeHelp: Every media server plugin that is switched on and set up is listed.
mediaServer.notRunning: The media server "{{id}}" is not running or not set up; Reelix files without it. Set its plugin up under Plugins, or choose another.
mediaServer.pathMapHelp: How the media server names the same folders: {{example}}
mediaServer.playersHelp: The order of the play links: infuse, swiftfin, jellyfin. Players not listed come after.

services.title: Services
services.description: Addresses of the services Reelix uses. Passwords and API keys go under Secrets.
services.subtitleSourcesHelp: Comma-separated, in order of preference: subhd, assrt, opensubtitles, subdl, gestdown, jimaku. Each is only asked for the languages and kinds of title it covers.
services.subtitleLanguagesHelp: Comma-separated, in order: zh, en, fr, ru, ja. Empty: follow the Reelix language (French and Russian also accept English).

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.intro: Values go straight to the server's secrets file. They are never shown again, and the agent never sees them.
secrets.placeholderReplace: Enter a new value to replace it

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.description: For services that are blocked or slow from home (TMDB, Telegram, subtitle sites).
proxy.useForHelp: Comma-separated services, e.g. tmdb, telegram, subhd, models.

models.title: Models
models.description: Each kind of work has a list of models, tried in order: if the first cannot answer, the next one is used. Models come from pi's sign-in and models file, and from magpie if set.

roleHelp.background: Follows, the nightly summary, subtitle searches. Empty: same as Chat.
roleHelp.glossary: Reads a whole subtitle for names and tone; a large-context model suits it. Empty: same as Background jobs.
roleHelp.translate: The bulk of a subtitle translation; a cheap, fast model suits it. Empty: same as Background jobs.
roleHelp.review: Checks a translation. A different model from the translator catches more. Empty: same as Translation: lines.

models.resting: Skipped for now after an error: {{models}}.
models.magpieHelp: Optional. A magpie gateway routes between providers and holds spending limits; its models and routing groups appear here as magpie/… . The gateway key goes under Secrets (magpie.api_key).
models.magpieSpent: Reelix's key has spent its {{limit}} {{period}}; it renews {{reset}}.
models.magpieAdmin: Changes: ask in chat. Each one is planned, checked, and put back if it breaks a role.
models.magpieReadOnly: Read only. To let Reelix change routing groups and providers, add a second magpie key allowed to manage magpie as the secret magpie.admin_key.
models.translatorHelp: Writes the lines of a subtitle translation; the glossary and the review stay with the models above. Every translator plugin that is switched on is listed.
models.translatorNotRunning: The translator "{{id}}" is not running; translations wait until it is. Switch its plugin on, or choose another.

limits.title: Limits and schedule
limits.description: Background work stops starting new model runs at the cap; chat is not capped.
limits.pluginDailyUsdHelp: For each plugin that uses your models, unless you set its own on its page. Resets at midnight.

agent.title: Preferences and what the agent learned
agent.description: Your taste in releases and subtitles, and things the agent has learned, live in notes the agent keeps. Change them by talking to it.
agent.editPrefsPrompt: Show me my preferences note, then let's change it:
agent.whatLearnedPrompt: What have you learned about my setup and taste so far? List your notes.

learned.title: Things I've learned
learned.description: Skills the agent wrote for itself.
learned.empty: Nothing yet. When the agent works something out about your setup (a site's quirks, a naming habit), it writes it down as a skill and it shows up here.
learned.changePrompt: About the skill "{{name}}" you wrote: change this:
learned.deleteDescription: The agent forgets what this skill told it.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: This device's own notifications when Reelix needs you. Tapping one opens the item in the Inbox.
notifications.sent: Sent. It should arrive in a moment.
notifications.needsHttps: Notifications need Reelix to be opened over HTTPS with a trusted certificate. On a NAS, the simplest way is Tailscale: run “tailscale serve --bg 7878” and open the https://….ts.net address it shows.
notifications.needsInstall: On iPhone and iPad, first add Reelix to the Home Screen: Share → Add to Home Screen. Open it from there, sign in, and come back here.
notifications.unsupported: This browser does not support notifications from web apps.
notifications.denied: Notifications are blocked for Reelix. Allow them in the system or browser settings, then come back.
notifications.pluginOff: The notifications plugin is switched off. Switch it on under Plugins.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.description: What is added to Reelix. Switching one on or off takes effect at once.
plugins.confirmTitle: Switch off {{id}} and what depends on it?
plugins.trialHelp: Its hooks run and Reelix records what they would change; nothing is applied. Its code still runs, with its network calls.
plugins.trialNone: No decisions yet in this trial.
plugins.trialFirst_one: would have changed the first candidate {{count}} time
plugins.trialFirst_other: would have changed the first candidate {{count}} times
plugins.toolsHelp: {{tools}}. Off: the assistant reaches its operations through the reelix tool only. Applies from the next conversation.
plugins.hookOrderHelp: In these steps each plugin changes what the one before it produced, so the order matters. The first runs first.
plugins.restartNeededManual: Restart Reelix to load: {{ids}}. Run `docker compose restart reelix`, or stop `reelix serve` and start it again.
plugins.installTitle: Install a plugin or skill pack
plugins.installHelp: A git URL pinned to a full commit id (…/repo.git#<commit>), npm:<name>@<exact version>, or a folder's full path. Nothing runs until you approve what it declares.
plugins.installing: Fetching it and its dependencies; install scripts are never run. This can take a minute.
plugins.reviewWarning: This is what the plugin says about itself; its code has not run. Once approved, its code runs inside Reelix and can do anything Reelix can.
plugins.reviewSkills: A skill pack: instructions for the assistant, and scripts it may run. It has no code that runs inside Reelix.
plugins.scriptsWarning: Contains scripts the assistant may run

flag.unmetered: Asks to run without a daily budget

plugins.nativeHelp: It has compiled dependencies. Reelix installs them only when ready-made binaries exist for this machine; nothing is compiled here.
plugins.diffTitle: What changed in what it declares
plugins.uninstallHelp: Its code is removed. Its settings, secrets and stored data are kept, so installing it again brings them back, unless you tick below.
plugins.deleteData: Also delete its settings, secrets and stored data
plugins.jobPromptHelp: What it adds to the assistant's instructions also reaches background jobs, where nobody is watching. Off unless you allow it.
plugins.setupMessage: I switched on the plugin {{id}}. Walk me through setting it up (the {{skill}} skill).
plugins.setupOffer: The assistant can walk you through setting up {{id}}.
plugins.setupStart: Set it up with the assistant

model.title: Your models
model.spent: Today: ${{usd}} of ${{budget}} ({{tokens}} tokens). Resets at midnight.
model.reached: The budget is used up: its model calls wait until midnight.

plugins.waitsForMissing: Waiting for the plugin {{id}} {{range}}: it is not installed
plugins.waitsForPlugin: Waiting for the plugin {{id}} {{range}}: there is {{version}}, {{state}}
plugins.proposalFailed: The proposal could not be handled
plugins.proposalHelp: Written by the agent. Nothing of it runs until you approve it; approving installs it as a folder, and it starts after a restart.
plugins.reviewWarningProcess: This is what the plugin says about itself; its code has not run. Once approved, its code runs in a process of its own with only its context. Node keeps it from Reelix's files and secrets, from starting programs and from compiled addons; Reelix's code in that process keeps it off the network except through Reelix. That holds a careless plugin, not yet a hostile one: install only code you trust.
plugins.runtimeProcess: in a process of its own
plugins.runtimeNoProcess: inside Reelix only (a raw pi extension or compiled code)
plugins.runtime: Run in a process of its own
plugins.runtimeHelp: Its code gets only its context. Node keeps it from Reelix's files, secrets and database and from starting programs; Reelix's code in that process keeps its network to Reelix's fetch, to the hosts it declares. That holds a careless plugin, not yet a hostile one. Off: it runs inside Reelix, where it can do anything Reelix can. Its author's default: {{default}}.
plugins.runtimeNotPossible: It cannot run in a process of its own: it has a raw pi extension or compiled dependencies.

channels.title: Chat channels
channels.description: Chat apps you talk to Reelix from.
channels.empty: No chat channel is set up. A chat app is set up on its plugin's page under Plugins (for Telegram: telegram).
channels.setUp: Linking and testing a chat app is done on its plugin's page under Plugins.
channels.mayApproveHelp: When on, your answers in this chat count as your approval, for example of a change to magpie. When off, such approvals are given in the web app.
channels.unlinkBody: The bot stops answering you until you link it again with a new code.
channels.sendFailed: The last message could not be sent ({{ago}}): {{error}}

folderPicker.title: Choose a folder
folderPicker.description: Folders inside the media folder ({{root}}), as Reelix sees them. Open a folder, then choose it.
folderPicker.truncated: Only the first 1000 folders are shown.

level.downloads: Choose the folder your downloader saves into. It must be on the same disk and shared folder as the library, so files can be hard-linked.
level.library: Choose the folder Jellyfin scans as this library: the one that holds a folder per title, not a title's own folder. For now each media type has one library folder.

folderPicker.tooDeep: This is a single title's folder (or one of its season folders). Go up to the folder that holds all the titles.
